endorsements.quote: All AI-generated content must be labeled and reviewed by a counselor before entering the clinical record, and counselors bear sole responsibility for evaluating discrepancies between AI-generated content and their own clinical assessment.
Classification depends on intended use, degree of clinical influence, and jurisdiction; organizations should determine it before deployment and after substantive system changes.

Lockout should remain in force until the emergency is resolved and the authorized clinical or supervisory professional completes the relevant handoff; if activation cannot be technically confirmed, AI output must remain disabled and human-only operation must continue.

A short-duration single-site pilot of lower-risk Tier 1 functions could evaluate documentation time, counselor workload, acceptability, review times, and technical reliability before expanding to higherimpact functions and clinical outcomes.

Tier 1 functions should be introduced in phases according to their potential clinical impact, beginning with lowconsequence documentation and administrative tasks before deploying functions that interpret caller language, generate clinical prompts, or influence follow-up.
Ultimate clinical responsibility remains with human counselors and supervisors.

Routine audits should review every interaction escalated to Step 5, that is, Step 4C, the Reality-Testing Override, clinical uncertainty, and unresolved gates, plus a sample of non-escalated interactions, with AI model updates revalidated rather than assumed unchanged.

Callers must be told immediately they are interacting with an automated system, offered silence as an alternative, and prioritized for human connection according to predefined, service-approved criteria rather than any AI interpretation of clinical state.

unlisted_practices: Notify callers at the start of the interaction, using a brief scripted statement, that AI is used to analyze their language or vocalization.
Offer callers an immediate opt-out from nonessential language or vocal-feature analysis, and log the opt-out independently.
Obtain caller consent to the specific automated follow-up channel and frequency before any automated contact, and allow withdrawal at any time.
Do not equate caller non-response with voluntary withdrawal; use predefined follow-up or escalation protocols instead.
Establish evidence of acceptable AI performance for each language and dialect in use, monitor it after implementation, and human-review translated content.
Prohibit AI from diagnosing, assigning suicide risk levels, determining disposition, initiating emergency interventions, or overriding clinicians.
Trigger an AI lockout with audit logging when an authorized clinician or supervisor declares an emergency.
Require supervisor review for high-risk, clinically uncertain, or unresolved-gate cases, with a documented backup process for reaching an alternate supervisor.
Set tiered review priorities and measure supervisor workload to prevent review backlogs.
Provide counselors with decompression time, supervisor check-in, and access to protected recovery time or peer support after emergency escalation.
Maintain incident logs distinguishing human error from system failure, and examine AI's role in adverse-event reviews without attributing automated culpability.
Conduct data protection impact assessments and implement role-based access controls, encryption, and audit logging for AI in crisis services.
Evaluate synthetic audio carefully before using it in place of prerecorded content for distressed callers.

screen.reason: The paper proposes a three-tier governance framework for integrating AI into crisis counseling workflows without reporting an empirical evaluation.
